newsitem.title: ITALY: Magistrates probe Olivetti's Caio, 3 others.
newsitem.headline: Magistrates probe Olivetti's Caio, 3 others.

text.p: Three other people are under investigation alongside Olivetti chief executive Francesco Caio in a probe by Italian magistrates of the crisis-hit company's balance sheets, judicial sources said on Tuesday.
The sources did not name the other three but said the preliminary inquiries were all linked to the group's 1996 first half results which were published two weeks ago.
Judicial sources said on Monday Caio would be questioned in the probe into the group's accounts by magistrates from the north western town of Ivrea, where Olivetti has its headquarters.
The questioning is the first step of an investigation which could lead to a full-scale criminal inquiry.

Olivetti, which has not broken even since 1990, reported a loss of 440.2 billion lira for the first half of 1996. A senior manager at the group resigned a day after the announcement saying he did not agree with all the figures in the financial statement.

Since then bourse watchdog Consob has been carrying out its own investigation into the state of Olivetti's financial affairs while the Ivrea magistrates' probe is the result of a complaint filed against the group by an association of small shareholders.
